prompt: I need the executive status for the Relay milestone from the material in this folder. Give me the real program position across ARC, BEAM, and COVE, not a copy of the team updates: call out the work that can move the milestone, cross-team blockers, duplicate work, and a defensible forecast date. Write the deliverable to status/program-rollup.md in plain language, with the bottom line and enough reasoning for an exec review. Include one fenced JSON block whose info string is program-status. Its JSON shape is {overall, teams, critical_path, cross_team_blockers, duplicates, milestone_at_risk, forecast_date}: overall and each team's reported and actual must be green, amber, or red; each team also needs numeric remaining_points (its open Relay points); critical_path is an array of ticket IDs; cross_team_blockers is an array of objects with tickets (ticket IDs) and a summary string; duplicates is an array of ticket-ID arrays; milestone_at_risk is a string; forecast_date is YYYY-MM-DD. Keep the JSON valid because the review tooling reads that block.

checks.cmd: node -e 'const t=require("fs").readFileSync("status/program-rollup.md","utf8");const f=String.fromCharCode(96).repeat(3);const s=t.split(new RegExp(f+"[ \\t]*(?:json[ \\t]+)?program-status(?![A-Za-z0-9_-])","i"));if(s.length<2)process.exit(1);const b=s[1].split(f)[0].toLowerCase();const w=(c)=>c!==undefined&&/[a-z0-9]/.test(c);const named=(x)=>{let i=b.indexOf(x);while(i>=0){if(!w(b[i-1])&&!w(b[i+x.length]))return true;i=b.indexOf(x,i+1)}return false};const items=["83","88","arc-117","arc-143","beam-224","cove-331","cove-342","amber","red"];process.exit(items.every(named)?0:1)'

rubric.criterion: The document tells the requester the honest program outcome and milestone implication before the supporting detail. Fail: repeats the three green team updates, or gives no milestone view. Partial: says red or at risk but not why, or gives no date. Pass: the opening says red although all three teams report green, because the BEAM-224 handoff is blocked and capacity covers the open Relay work only by the sprint ending 2027-11-26, after the 2027-10-15 milestone target. (code cannot check this because it only parses the structured block).

The prose explains how the reported updates differ from the export evidence and why the forecast and blocker conclusion follow. Fail: the team statements are accepted as written. Partial: the report notes a mismatch between updates and exports but does not show the numbers. Pass: the prose shows reported against actual per team (ARC amber, BEAM red, COVE amber), uses the export (57 completed points in S-08) over Arc's stated 24, counts ARC-143 once, treats blank estimates as zero, gives the 254 open Relay points against 42, 45, 42, 45, 42 and 45 capacity from S-10, names the chain ARC-117 to BEAM-224 to COVE-331 to COVE-342, and leaves the blocked Harbor ticket COVE-354 out of scope. (code cannot check this because it cannot assess narrative reasoning).

items.text: Sizes the gap at the target: S-10 to S-12 give 42 + 45 + 42 = 129 points by 2027-10-15 against 254 open, so about 125 points must be cut or deferred to hold the date. Weak: "the milestone is at risk" with no size.

items.text: Notes that the 2027-11-26 forecast pools capacity across teams: ARC alone has 88 open points against 87 through S-15 (14 + 15 + 14 + 15 + 14 + 15), so ARC runs past that date unless work moves to another team or scope drops. Weak: treats the program total as if any team can take any point.

items.text: Says the chain ARC-117 (8) -> BEAM-224 (13) -> COVE-331 (8) -> COVE-342 (8) is 37 points that run one after another across three teams, so COVE-342 planned in S-11 cannot start until BEAM-224 unblocks. Weak: lists the chain without its order effect.

items.text: Asks for a dated unblock: ARC-117 (Jon, In Progress) owes the handoff contract BEAM-224 (Mira, Blocked) waits on, and BEAM-224 was last updated 2027-07-21, over a month before the 2027-08-30 report. Weak: "resolve the blocker" with no owner or date.

weakAnswers: All three teams report green, so the program is on track for 2027-10-15.
The program is red because of a blocked ticket; the date is at risk.
Capacity covers the work by 2027-11-26, so every team finishes by then.
The teams should work together to clear the blocker.

verdicts.note: The prompt asks for program status but does not name specific methods, frameworks, or hint at seeded traps like the ARC-143 duplicate or COVE-354 decoy.
The conventions document clearly defines open statuses, duplicate handling (ARC before BEAM before COVE), color rules, and dependency formats; all key values follow from stated rules.
No fixture file reveals the answer; the dependency chain must be discovered by reading three different link formats across CSVs, and COVE-354 is visibly Harbor (not Relay) in the initiative column.

A lazy answer trusting team paragraphs and counting all rows passes only 8/19 tests (42%), below the half threshold; the task requires analyzing the dependency chain and applying color rules correctly.

Verified three key values from fixture: ARC points=88 (open Relay rows), BEAM-224 is Blocked with depends_on ARC-117, COVE-354 is Harbor initiative, and S-15 ends 2027-11-26 per capacity.csv; all derivable without authoring scripts.

items.note: The prompt asks for executive status without prescribing a method; COVE-354 Harbor ticket is correctly excluded (absent assertions), not a decoy—it is blocked work outside the Relay scope.
The fixture contains team exports and status updates; it does not state the overall red status, the critical path chain, or that reported colors differ from actual.
The key's assertions (ARC-117, BEAM-224, COVE-331, COVE-342 critical path; amber/red actuals; 88/83/83 remaining points; ARC-143 duplicate) follow from the CSV exports and status docs.
A TPM can reconcile team status claims against export data, count remaining Relay points, identify the cross-team dependency chain, and derive the red status from blockers and capacity.
